```go
func w28Gen(t *testing.T, seed uint64, chains []int, pos []int, bscale float64, mimo bool, big float64) (sys, oracle *System) {
	t.Helper()
	rng := rand.New(rand.NewPCG(seed, 2828))
	nf := 1 + rng.IntN(3)
	f, w := make([]float64, nf), make([]float64, nf)
	for i := range nf {
		f[i], w[i] = rng.NormFloat64(), 0.5+rng.Float64()
	}
	f[0] = math.Copysign(math.Pow(10, big+(6-big)*rng.Float64()), rng.NormFloat64())
	m, p := 1, 1
	if mimo {
		m, p = 1+rng.IntN(3), 1+rng.IntN(3)
	}
	n := nf
	for _, k := range chains {
		n += k
	}
	F, W := mat.NewDense(n, n, nil), mat.NewDense(n, n, nil)
	b, c, D := mat.NewDense(n, m, nil), mat.NewDense(p, n, nil), mat.NewDense(p, m, nil)
	for i := range nf {
		F.Set(i, i, f[i])
		W.Set(i, i, w[i])
		for j := range m {
			b.Set(i, j, rng.NormFloat64())
		}
		for j := range p {
			c.Set(j, i, rng.NormFloat64())
		}
	}
	o := nf
	for _, k := range chains {
		for i := range k {
			F.Set(o+i, o+i, 1)
			if i+1 < k {
				W.Set(o+i, o+i+1, 1)
			}
			for j := range p {
				c.Set(j, o+i, rng.NormFloat64())
			}
			in := false
			for _, q := range pos {
				in = in || q == i
			}
			for j := range m {
				v := rng.NormFloat64()
				switch {
				case i == 0:
					b.Set(o+i, j, v)
				case in:
					b.Set(o+i, j, v*bscale)
				}
			}
		}
		o += k
	}
	for i := range p {
		for j := range m {
			D.Set(i, j, rng.NormFloat64())
		}
	}
	gauss := func() *mat.Dense {
		g := mat.NewDense(n, n, nil)
		for i := range n {
			for j := range n {
				g.Set(i, j, rng.NormFloat64())
			}
		}
		return g
	}
	U, V := gauss(), gauss()
	var T, A, E, B, C mat.Dense
	T.Mul(U, F)
	A.Mul(&T, V)
	T.Mul(U, W)
	E.Mul(&T, V)
	B.Mul(U, b)
	C.Mul(c, V)
	var err error
	if sys, err = NewDescriptor(&A, &B, &C, D, &E, 0); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if oracle, err = NewDescriptor(F, b, c, D, W, 0); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return sys, oracle
}
```

### A.3 C1 jitter certificate (probe)

```go
type l4bEig struct {
	w    complex128
	move float64
	inf  bool
}

func l4bQZ(A, E *mat.Dense) ([]complex128, []bool, bool) {
	n, _ := A.Dims()
	ar, er := A.RawMatrix(), E.RawMatrix()
	alphar, alphai, beta, ok := qzEigenvalues(n, ar.Data, ar.Stride, er.Data, er.Stride)
	if !ok {
		return nil, nil, false
	}
	infTol := qzInfiniteTol(100*float64(n)*eps(), mat.Norm(A, 2), mat.Norm(E, 2))
	w := make([]complex128, n)
	inf := make([]bool, n)
	for i := range n {
		inf[i] = qzInfinite(alphar[i], alphai[i], beta[i], infTol)
		if !inf[i] {
			w[i] = complex(alphar[i]/beta[i], alphai[i]/beta[i])
		}
	}
	return w, inf, true
}

func l4bJitterCert(A, E *mat.Dense) ([]l4bEig, bool) {
	w, inf, ok := l4bQZ(A, E)
	if !ok {
		return nil, false
	}
	out := make([]l4bEig, len(w))
	for i := range w {
		out[i] = l4bEig{w: w[i], inf: inf[i]}
	}
	rng := rand.New(rand.NewPCG(3, 5))
	jitter := func(m *mat.Dense) *mat.Dense {
		c := mat.DenseCopyOf(m)
		raw := c.RawMatrix()
		for i := range raw.Rows {
			row := raw.Data[i*raw.Stride : i*raw.Stride+raw.Cols]
			for j := range row {
				row[j] *= 1 + 4*eps()*(2*rng.Float64()-1)
			}
		}
		return c
	}
	for range leakDraws {
		g, ginf, gok := l4bQZ(jitter(A), jitter(E))
		if !gok {
			return nil, false
		}
		for i := range out {
			if out[i].inf {
				continue
			}
			best := math.Inf(1)
			for j := range g {
				if !ginf[j] {
					best = min(best, cmplx.Abs(g[j]-out[i].w)/cmplx.Abs(out[i].w))
				}
			}
			out[i].move = max(out[i].move, best)
		}
	}
	return out, true
}

func l4bCertCount(es []l4bEig) int {
	c := 0
	for _, e := range es {
		if !e.inf && e.move <= leakStableTol {
			c++
		}
	}
	return c
}

```

### A.4 O4 classifier at 2^-k

It uses `pencilDetPoly`, `polyRoots`, `bcAbs2`, `bcSub` and `polyRootPrec` from `descriptor_pole_count_oracle_test.go` on origin/parked/descriptor-elt76f-staircase 76a7a1e. The probe calls `l4bClassify(n, a, e, 53, seed)` for seeds 100, 101 and 102.

```go
func l4bClassify(n int, a, e []float64, k uint, seed uint64) poleCountSensitivity {
	rat := func(x []float64, pert *rand.Rand) []*big.Rat {
		out := make([]*big.Rat, len(x))
		for i, v := range x {
			out[i] = new(big.Rat).SetFloat64(v)
			if pert != nil {
				f := new(big.Rat).SetInt64(1)
				d := new(big.Rat).SetFrac(big.NewInt(1), new(big.Int).Lsh(big.NewInt(1), k))
				if pert.IntN(2) == 0 {
					f.Add(f, d)
				} else {
					f.Sub(f, d)
				}
				out[i].Mul(out[i], f)
			}
		}
		return out
	}
	rng := rand.New(rand.NewPCG(seed, 53))
	z0, ok0 := polyRoots(pencilDetPoly(n, rat(a, nil), rat(e, nil)))
	z1, ok1 := polyRoots(pencilDetPoly(n, rat(a, rng), rat(e, rng)))
	out := poleCountSensitivity{OK: ok0 && ok1}
	used := make([]bool, len(z1))
	for _, r := range z0 {
		best, bd := -1, (*big.Float)(nil)
		for j, q := range z1 {
			if used[j] {
				continue
			}
			if d := bcAbs2(bcSub(r, q)); best < 0 || d.Cmp(bd) < 0 {
				best, bd = j, d
			}
		}
		used[best] = true
		rel := new(big.Float).SetPrec(polyRootPrec).Quo(bd, bcAbs2(r))
		f, _ := rel.Float64()
		out.Roots = append(out.Roots, r.complex128())
		out.S = append(out.S, math.Sqrt(f))
	}
	return out
}
```

title: DECISION (decided, live): TunePIDFRD certification done-bar for sampled FRD data (supersedes pruned XTCC7X)
body:
Re-filed 2026-10-26 from XTCC7X (pruned; quoted verbatim from git f86231f:.ergo/backlog.jsonl). DECISION record: kept as draft so it is never pruned or picked up as ready work. Amendments below are part of the operative bar.

## Original (XTCC7X, 2026-10-25)
DECIDED 2026-10-25 (advisor, per advisor-for-decisions; coordinator request). Scope: TunePIDFRD certification on sampled FRD data. Not TunePID (HEOZ5K, YRNRQP, ZHTUBP, PC4MF4, S7ERV4 out of scope).

MATLAB basis: pidtune doc defines info.Stable only as "1 if the closed loop is stable, and 0 otherwise"; for frd plants it relies on the user-supplied unstable-pole count (pidtuneOptions) and does not say how Stable is verified from samples. So the certified flag is stricter than MATLAB and the bar is ours; only 3N3NG2 (never fail, return uncertified with warning) is parity. https://www.mathworks.com/help/control/ref/dynamicsystem.pidtune.html

1. Certified = Nyquist count known from data AND every crossing used for reported margins read from a resolved step. Does not mean the PM target was met (AchievedPhaseMargin < target is allowed and visible).
2. Resolved step: trusted fit (pidTuningFRDTrusted(StepFits)), or smooth-step cubic gate passes (pidTuningFRDSmoothCrossing), or chord with no |L|-1 sign change and |L|-1 not within eps of 0 at either end. Band ends anchored per pidTuningFRDTopFlat / pidTuningFRDLowCrossings.
3. Guarantees on a CERTIFIED design (violation = bug, checked vs dense oracle): oracle-stable; reported PM <= dense PM + 1.5 deg; reported |S| >= dense peak / 1.05 (and certified implies dense |S| <= 4 within that slack); HARD RULE: design and error identical to base for every oracle-robust case. Certification granted on an unresolved step is a bug.
4. Documented limits (close, don't fix): any margin discrepancy on an UNCERTIFIED design; loss of certification when a pole/zero sits within ~10x above hi or below lo; loss of certification on noisy data; reporting error inside tolerance (incl. under-reports).
5. Search stays chord-based. A search change is an optional separate CORE task whose acceptance is zero design changes among oracle-robust cases in the 2800-case sweep.
6. Done-bar test: one persistent sweep test over fixed seeds of the standard families asserting item 3 for every certified design; skipSlowUnderRace.
Filing cutoff: no new TunePIDFRD task unless it violates item 3 on a certified design or certifies an unresolved step. Everything else goes into the sweep summary as a limit.
Folds 7WK6K5 (its search items = item 5).

## Amendment 1 (2026-10-26, PR #370, accepted by coordinator/advisor): item 2 widened for chord crossings
A chord crossing strictly inside an unmarked step counts as RESOLVED if any of: a step fit read a crossing in that step (lone fits included); trusted StepFits exist; the smooth-step cubic gate passes; or no polynomial reading (chord at w, cubic, both quadratics through neighbouring samples; non-crossing interpolants ignored) is more than 1.5 deg below the achieved margin. Otherwise the design is uncertified ("not certified ... nor its margins"). Reason: the literal item-2 reading uncertified ~10% of accurate certified designs (19/136 res, 7/49 sparse, 1/93 strict); the widened rule loses only violators plus item-4 limit cases.

## Amendment 2 (2026-10-26, QHMGQL ruling, coordinator/advisor)
Item 4 "limits" cover only what the certifier REPORTS as unknown (uncertified). They never excuse a design the certifier certified: any certified design violating item 3 is a CORE bug, wherever the hidden dynamics sit (e.g. resonance beyond the ~10x TopFlat zone). For ideal-derivative (Tf=0) designs: do not anchor/certify the Markov end unless |L(inf)| is well below 1; gains unchanged, uncertified with warning (3N3NG2), never fail, never estimate true PM from data lacking the resonance. Guardrail: 2600-case base-vs-branch sweep; if accurate ideal-PID designs lose certification beyond a handful, narrow the gate (e.g. tie the |L(inf)| threshold to TopFlat curvature) rather than loosen the bar.

## Note
Decision tasks are not pruned: keep them as drafts (never done), so `ergo prune` cannot remove them.

## Amendment 3 (2026-10-26, QHMGQL ruling, coordinator/advisor): ideal-derivative Markov end is never certified
For continuous ideal-derivative designs (Tf = 0, Kd != 0) the Markov end 1 + Kd*m is never certified from sampled data; the design is returned unchanged with a "not certified" warning that names the cause (no roll-off) and suggests PIDF (Tf > 0) (3N3NG2). Documented limit of band-limited data: L does not roll off, so a pole pair of damping zeta anywhere above the band lifts |L| by about 1/(2 zeta), and band-limited samples bound neither zeta nor the distance. Rejected alternative: a zeta_min floor (threshold 2*zeta_min) is a heuristic constant no reference library uses (matlab-parity rule) and would knowingly admit certified violators (amendment 2).
Evidence (wave 30, fix/pid-wave30): 3300 seeded base-vs-branch cases (strict, resonance, sparse, top-cut, resonance-sparse x520, plus hidden-pair family PCG 7702): 0 design or error changes; certified done-bar violators 24 on base -> 0 of 3300 on branch. Cost: 43 accurate ideal-D designs in the 2600 standard cases lose certification (~9.4% of base-certified), still returned with the warning. The narrower gate (|L(inf)|<=0.5 or TopFlat bend<=TopCurvature/3) leaked 42/1200 hidden-pair violators.

The shipped noiseGainIll gate (eps-scaled forward-error bound of G*Kw = B'X, OR cond(E)*eps > newtonTol) is a partial bound. title: DECISION (decided, live): descriptor E rank = MATLAB rank (n*eps(sigma_1)) via descriptorRank; luNearSingular never declares E deficient
body:
DECIDED 2026-10-26 (advisor, per advisor-for-decisions). DECISION record: kept as draft so it is never pruned.

Rule: the numerical rank of a descriptor E is MATLAB rank(E): default tolerance max(size(E))*eps(norm(E)) = n*eps(sigma_1) on the singular values (https://www.mathworks.com/help/matlab/ref/rank.html). In controlsys this is exactly descriptorRank(sv, sv[0], n, full=true) (floor n*ulp(sigma_1)), already the D62TAA SLICOT/MATLAB rule. It is the only arbiter of "E singular / rank deficient" for ToExplicit, TransferFunction, IsProper, Step and the descriptor reduction.

luNearSingular (matutil.go: cond estimate * eps >= 1, or NaN/Inf) is a heuristic and must NOT declare E rank deficient ahead of the SVD rule. It may stay only as a conservative cheap exit in the other direction (lu.Cond()*10n^2*eps < 1 => full rank, as in eRankDeficient) or for an exact zero pivot. Call sites that use luNearSingular as a rank decision on E fall under this ruling: state_space_utils.go eRankDeficient (line ~99), descriptor.go ~97/116/652/1044 (check each: E rank vs solve-conditioning use). Non-descriptor uses (canon, controller, inv, convert, transform, matrix_equation_problem, conversion_delay) are solve-conditioning checks, out of scope.
FreqResponse solves (sE-A) directly and does not use E rank; confirm when implementing.

Consequence: models with sigma_n ~ eps*sigma_1 (k ~ 0.8-1.2 in rv30rNSE) read full rank, as MATLAB does. VDATJL (seed 1624 TF error) is this symptom and is folded into the implementation task. More near-boundary models then flow through the stiff explicit path, so WOIVWF (Step off for ill-conditioned E) may grow in count: that is MATLAB ss(dss) parity, not a regression.
Implementation: CORE task filed separately; queue after #374 (touches state_space_utils.go, transfer.go).

Scope note (wave 33): Low priority: requireNonsingular in descriptor.go:116 (lqr/icare-type entry points through newControllerObserverPolicy) still rejects E on luNearSingular (cond*eps >= 1) when MATLAB rank(E) is full. The coordinator can extend RL6IT7 there if MATLAB lqr(dss) parity calls for it. The likely trigger is the existing test model fullRankNearSingularE(t, 2.46e-15) in descriptor_e_rank_test.go passed to an lqr/kalman entry point. Not run, so whether MATLAB itself rejects this E is not established. Pending owner/advisor decision whether lqr/kalman/lqg descriptor entry points (requireNonsingular, descriptor.go:116) follow this rule; needs Riccati accuracy evidence before moving models from error to value.

## Amendment 1 (2026-10-26, advisor; coordinator asked): lqr/kalman/lqg descriptor entry points
MATLAB basis: lqr Tips: "lqr supports descriptor models with nonsingular E"; S is the Riccati solution "for the equivalent explicit state-space model" (https://www.mathworks.com/help/control/ref/lti.lqr.html). MATLAB states no rank test, so "nonsingular" follows this decision: MATLAB rank(E) full = nonsingular.
Ruling: descriptorPolicy.requireNonsingular (descriptor.go, used by newControllerObserverPolicy for Lqr/Kalman/Lqg/Lqi family) uses the RL6IT7 rule (descriptorRank full=true), not luNearSingular. Admission is not a value: newly admitted models go through the E-aware Riccati path (model E passed to Care/Dare), and the design is returned only if verifyRiccati certifies it honestly (ZLHTCH/D3WPCL honesty rule); otherwise ErrDescriptorSingular/ErrNoStabilizing as before. No explicit E^-1 fold for these.
Implementation: CORE task (filed separately); guardrail: rv30rNSE-class sweep k in [0.5,2] through Lqr/Kalman/Lqg vs 320-bit oracle, assert Accuracy honesty, zero correct->wrong, report error->value counts. Queue after #376 (descriptor.go) and D3WPCL (riccati.go) merge.

## Amendment 2 (2026-10-26, advisor; supersedes amendment 1 admission rule): Riccati entry points
Evidence (wave 35, M23EGI): rejecting on MATLAB rank alone strands 50+ base Lqr values that the 320-bit oracle shows correct AND robust to eps perturbations of E (window B: MATLAB rank deficient by a hair, LU cond*eps<1). No value->error outranks amendment 1.
Rule: for IsProper/TF/Step/ToExplicit, MATLAB rank alone decides (E rank IS the answer). For Riccati entry points (descriptorPolicy.requireNonsingular, riccatiDescriptor), "nonsingular E" is a solver precondition that MATLAB lqr states without a tolerance: admit when MATLAB rank is full OR LU cond*eps<1 (reject only when both say singular). Union of two existing rules, no new constant. Honesty comes from the gates, not admission: verifyRiccati + nearSingularEGate cancellation screen + Kalman dual via plantE. Known exception: Kalmd keeps the old LU rejection (folds E^-1 unverified).
Lqi: judge the PLANT E, not blkdiag(E,I): rank(blkdiag(E,I)) = rank(E)+p exactly; the augmented tolerance (n+p)*eps*max(sigma1,1) is a scaling artifact when sigma1(E)<1. Implementation is a follow-up task in controller.go.

## Amendment 3 (2026-10-26, advisor; from YW5B4U amendment 1, PR #380): Stabsep/Modsep stiff full-rank mode
Evidence (PR #380): a descriptor G1 = (S11, T11) carrying the stiff mode has t_ii ~3e-16 and fails MATLAB rank by the same RL6IT7 rule that made the mode finite, so Poles(G1) would drop it again (the EJYYFD class one level down). Review: 2400 broad + 1983 targeted cases, native and amd64, zero regressions; G1+G2 matches the pencil to 1e-9 at five frequencies.
Principle: the invariant governs over the mechanism. A representation that fails the rule that made the mode finite cannot carry that mode.
Rule:
1. A stiff beta=0 mode of a full-rank E is added to the part isGroup1(lambda) selects as an explicit decoupled state (lambda, b/beta, c). G1 stays explicit; no type change for any model base handled correctly. MATLAB "same type as G" holds in the class sense (dss is ss).
2. G2 becomes explicit only under the decomposeGeneralized trigger, quoted verbatim:
   if sawInfinite && nf == a.RawMatrix().Rows {
       if lambda, ok := stiffFullRankPole(sys.A, sys.E); ok && (n1 > 0 || isGroup1(lambda)) {
   i.e. the selector rejected a beta~0 mode AND deflateInfinite deflated nothing (full-rank E). On a full-rank E that trigger is exactly "base dropped a finite pole", so no model base handled correctly enters this path.
Residual: tiny nonzero beta outside the class is tracked under HK6D3N.

## Amendment 4 (2026-10-27, advisor; HK6D3N, PR wave 37): Stabsep/Modsep tiny nonzero beta
Same principle as amendment 3, applied to the tiny-nonzero-beta case the beta=0 wording did not cover. Gate quoted verbatim from decomposeGeneralized:
    if n := nf; !sawInfinite && n == a.RawMatrix().Rows && n1 < n &&
        descriptorERankDeficient(extractModalBlock(t, n, n1, n, n1, n)) && !descriptorERankDeficient(sys.E) {
        if lambda, tol, ok := stiffTinyBetaPole(sys.A, sys.E); ok {
            if g1, g2, ok := splitStiffFullRank(...); ok && (g2.E == nil || !descriptorERankDeficient(g2.E)) {
i.e. G2's T22 fails MATLAB rank while sys.E does not; accepted only if the resulting G2 is not rank deficient; otherwise base. It can only restore a dropped pole. Evidence: 1.81M op lines native + 308k amd64, 37+8 changed lines, all restoring a dropped pole, 0 IsStable flips on sys or parts, 0 errors.
stiffRatioGap (new constant, 10x) survives the no-invented-constants rule only because it decides WHETHER TO ATTEMPT the repair (which eigenvalue is the isolated stiff one), never WHAT THE ANSWER IS: the result is checked by the rank invariant and falls back to base.

## Amendment 5 (2026-10-27, advisor; HK6D3N): scope of "agree with the explicit model"
The EJYYFD/amendment-3 agreement tiebreak was for the beta=0 deflation artifact (QZ the broken party, finiteness from MATLAB rank). It means "do not drop a finite mode", not "Poles inherits the fold's values". Poles/IsStable are the pencil (MATLAB pole(dss) = eig(A,E)). The agreement rule covers E rank and finite-mode retention, not pole values.
ToExplicit (E^-1 A fold): when ||E^-1 A|| ~ 1/eps any float64 rounding moves slow eigenvalues O(1); a representation limit of the explicit form. MATLAB ss(sys,'explicit') documents no alternative method (https://www.mathworks.com/help/control/ref/ss.html), so ToExplicit's output stays the explicit model by contract and is a documented limit. HK6D3N evidence: 822 (oracle agrees with Poles/QZ, stable) : 0 (agrees with fold) : 7 (flips under eps perturbation); 0 stiff-sign disagreements in 55k+ models. Step/C2D, which simulate the fold, are handled under WOIVWF (CORE).

Amendment 6 (advisor + coordinator ruling, wave 38 WOIVWF): descriptor-native routing of full-rank ill-conditioned E. Impulse (time domain) routes at the stiffPencilSplit gate (LU cond(E) >= 1e4 before and after equilibration, full MATLAB rank): the fold impulse is wrong from 1e4 (2799 of 2809 well-posed sweep rows), so case (b), correctness wins. C2D (all methods except matched), Step and zero-x0 Lsim route only when the raw LU cond(E) >= foldAccurateECond = 1e6 (convert.go foldInaccurateParts), because the LU fold is within tolerance in [1e4, 1e6): C2D 324 fold-ok vs 1 fold-wrong, Step 295 vs 2 (9300-model sweep, 320-bit pencil oracle), so case (a). This brings mild-cond C2D from 2.4x to 1.34x vs base. Raw (not equilibrated) cond is the feature, because ToExplicit factorizes the raw E. Matched C2D uses the pencil transfer function whenever stiffDescriptorParts applies.
Amendment 7: Step/C2D use splitFastPencil (3+ parts); TransferFunction stays two-part stiffExplicitParts until task UOFXRA unifies them.
Amendment 8: stiffModalHold changes explicit-model C2D ZOH/FOH/impulse and Step (rho(A)*dt >= 1e3, quasi-triangular or all-stiff A; dense mixed-mode unchanged). Accepted on a 6000-model explicit sweep (0 correct->wrong) and a fohKernel-caller probe (C2D FOH, C2DMap FOH, fractional-delay FOH channel/LFT, D2C FOH: 0 correct->wrong, 0 value->error vs base). Fractional-delay FOH stays wrong on both trees (task RR43HG).

Amendment 9 (advisor, wave 45 AZUMSC): Initial and Lsim with nonzero x0 route at the same gate as Step and zero-x0 Lsim: raw LU cond(E) >= foldAccurateECond (1e6, via foldInaccurateParts/foldInaccurateContinuous), no I/O delay, no LFT. This supersedes am.6's "zero-x0" qualifier. Reasons: Lsim must not switch routes between x0=0 and x0=eps; the fold's Initial was < 1e-7 on 283/283 well-posed models in [1e4, 1e6); round 2 found 0 correct->wrong in 3100 cases. Mechanism: a separate pencil split of the free response (stiffFreeParts/addStiffFreeSamples), not an A*x0 step augmentation. That augmentation cancels C*x0 against C*z in the tail, and its error grew with |x0| (gen 1331: 1.2e-5, now 1.0e-8). Delayed C2D: non-matched methods build a parallel explicit model (stiffDescriptorExplicit, realSchurPart per am.8) at the same 1e6 gate. Matched with delays keeps the descriptor at the existing delay-free matched route (stiffDescriptorParts) and returns the delay-free result times z^-k.

### am.10 (wave 47, XWFTRV; advisor ruling) — supersedes am.9's "no I/O delay" qualifier
am.6/am.9 routing (Impulse at stiffPencilSplit; Step/Lsim/Initial at raw LU cond(E) >= 1e6) applies with I/O delays (no LFT), via ioDelayFreeCore. Impulse samples shifted parts exactly (shiftedStiffImpulse); free response shifts per OutputDelay; Delay matrix without I/O split still ErrDelayUnsupported. Step/Lsim with off-grid delays carry RR43HG residue (test stepTol 1e-5; tighten to 1e-7 after RR43HG). Side effect: base's auto horizon collapsed to the delay on delayed stiff models; fixed.

Wave 38 probe. title: Pidtune ~6-8x slower on simple auto calls since AUOTFB first-design gate (owner decision on gate grid)
body:
Found in wave 10 (PR pending, branch fix/wave10).

Perf (CR7GLM, caused by AUOTFB): newPidtuneGate now runs on every automatic Pidtune call. It evaluates the plant about 3000 times (sens grid about 230 points/decade, cross grid 100/decade, no shared points, band floor*1e-3 to wc*1e3). Result: about 8x slower on BenchmarkPidtune_PI/PID/PIDF (93us to 760us, 25KB to 388KB/op) and +66% on the continuous-delay sweep. Options: share or interpolate the sens and cross plant samples, cheaper pole-residue evaluation of the SISO plant on the grids, or lazy top-down |S| scanning. Files: pidtune.go (newPidtuneGate, pidtuneGate.sensitivityOver, crossExcess). Repro: go run ./scripts/benchcmp -base 8cfed86 -candidate 027664e -bench Pidtune.

Pidtune slowdown on simple plants from 027664e (AUOTFB first-design gate). Repro: go run ./scripts/benchcmp -base 8cfed86 -candidate 027664e -bench Pidtune. Evidence, 8cfed86 to HEAD: Pidtune_PI 80 us to 711 us (+787%), PID +836%, PIDF +751%, PidtuneFastSampled/O2 42 us to 797 us (+1795%), O5 +429%, Delayed/PI +185%, Delayed/PD 1.0 ms to 15 ms (+1358%), Delayed/PIDF +142%; B/op 25 KB to 388 KB, allocs/op +42% to +60% (Delayed/PD +2190%, of which my commits recover 8.6%). The 027664e-vs-HEAD benchcmp shows my commits leave time unchanged, so this all comes from 027664e. Cause: every automatic first design now builds newPidtuneGate, which samples about 9+ decades ([floor*1e-3, wc*1e3]) even when the design then passes. Files: pidtune.go (Pidtune, run.design(wc, sign, auto), newPidtuneGate). Narrowing the band or building the gate lazily could change gate verdicts, so this is an owner decision; not fixed.

Pidtune small automatic calls still cost about 470us vs 77us on 8cfed86 (Pidtune_PI/PID/PIDF, FastSampled ~2.6x). Cause: AUOTFB gates every auto first design on the full back-off gate grid, [floor*1e-3, wc*1e3] at 1% steps (about 2100 plant solves, pidtune.go newPidtuneGate). Lowering it means building the first design's grid lazily or narrowing it, which changes verdicts on some plants; that needs an owner decision.

Perf: BenchmarkPidtune_Delayed/PD (0.3s-1/(s+1)^4, input delay 5, PD, wc=0) is 1.1-1.2ms on base and about 18-28ms now. The gated first design (|S| 7.6) fails, all 60 back-off steps run gate checks and fail, then the ungated first design is returned as the fallback. A faster failing gate path or an earlier stop (e.g. when |S| rises steadily as wc drops) would recover this. File: pidtune.go (Pidtune back-off loop).

Perf (minor, existing pattern): on the reflected-delay path, r.screened(wc) and checkPidtuneStability each call screen.at(wc, family), which builds pidTuningDelayStability state twice per step that reaches Nyquist. The same double call happens on the non-delay gated path (r.gated(pid, wc, r.screened(wc))). Files: pidtune.go (pidtuneRun.check), pid_tuning.go (pidStabilityScreen.at).

BenchmarkPidtune_BackoffFail/GateP is +7% (3.52 to 3.77 ms) after the crossover scan moved to the finer |S| grid (16add00). Repro: benchcmp -base b0e01b5 -candidate 9b2e8d4 -bench ^BenchmarkPidtune. Most of it is bisection and golden-section refinement calls into the memoized p.at during back-off steps that fail anyway.


Wave 13 reports folded in:

[w13 #60] CORE (perf): MaxEvaluations does not bound TunePID runtime on delayed lightly damped plants. Repro: s := fzDecode(t, 0x80, [0,3,0.3,4,0,0,6,0,-1,-3,0.8,-3.5,-10,52,-10,-10]) gives modes ζ=0.1 at 1 rad/s and ζ=0.01 at 2 rad/s, with a 19.95 s output delay. TunePID(PIDF, MaxEvaluations:512) takes 51 s and returns Unattainable. With damp=5 (ζ=1e-3) it takes 169 s. With a 3.16 s delay it takes 0.3 s. Pidtune on the same plant takes 4 ms and returns a design. Related: Pidtune takes about 50 s on fzDecode(0x80, [6,11,0.3,0.5,0,0,6,-7,-0.5,-30,0.2,0.5,38,-100,-10,-10]) (a ζ=1e-5 mode at 1e4 rad/s, 20 s input delay). title: DECISION (decided, live): Riccati result honesty rule (certified-wrong definition, error->certified-wrong forbidden)
body:
DECIDED (advisor, 2026-10-27; applied since wave 31, previously only in track-decision strings). DECISION record: kept as draft so it is never pruned.

Riccati result honesty rule (Care/Dare/Lqr/Dlqr/Kalman/Lqg/Lqi and descriptor variants):
1. Certified-wrong = Accuracy 0 with error (X or K, vs 320-bit SDA doubling X and 320-bit gain K) > max(newtonTol ~1e-8, a few x the oracle's own eps-perturbation sensitivity). Errors inside that band are the documented Accuracy-0 contract, not violations.
2. error -> certified-wrong is FORBIDDEN, even when the same defect exists elsewhere on base.
3. certified-wrong -> error, and Accuracy 0 -> Accuracy 1, are always allowed (honest direction).
4. No value -> error where base was correct and robust.
5. With R>0 the optimal K is unique (MATLAB idare/dare): K, not only the closed loop, must match the 320-bit gain.
Reviewers count error->certified-wrong rows explicitly by this definition every wave and block if nonzero.
Refinements (XXC5C2 refix, accepted): the K tolerance is the gain's move under X(1 +/- eps) plus a componentwise conditioning bound (normwise was ~1e3 pessimistic); a gain double-double cannot resolve to 1e-4 is not certified.

Amendment 1 (advisor, wave 39 5MLDJ6): Accuracy 0 certifies the PAIR (X, K). Dare may move both to X one Newton step on (re-certified by Newton) with K = double-double gain of that X, only if A-BK is stable and gainMiss passes; else Accuracy 1. Substituting K without re-certifying X is forbidden (COKNFU ungated experiment: seed 83 ok->certwrong). Evidence: sweeps 16000 arm64 / 6000 amd64 rows, 0 err->certwrong, 0 ok->certwrong, 0 value->error. Test tolerances may scale with the measured gain move per ulp of X (dareGainUlpMove).
Amendment 2 (advisor, wave 39): gainTol = 1e-6 is the current K floor, a documented detector limit (same shape as RL6IT7 am.5). Rows with K error < 1e-6 but >> K sensitivity are known certified-wrong by the strict letter of rule 1; tracked in the sensitivity-aware gainTol task, not a per-wave block.

Amendment 3 (advisor, wave 40 5AFLTD/7UDJQH): where float64 cannot hold X to the gain's precision (cond(E)*eps regime), am.1's "double-double gain of a re-certified X" may be the gain of a double-double Newton/Hewer iterate converged to newtonRefineTol; the returned X stays the certified float64 iterate (replacing it lost re-certification: seed 257, 22 acc1->err). K and E'XE from that dd iterate are TERMINAL: no later explicit-path check (rLost -> gainOfX -> refined) may replace them with a gain of the float64 X. Accuracy 1 -> certified-wrong is FORBIDDEN, same class as error -> certified-wrong (wave-40 review-2 block: seed 3559 discrete Kalman, cond(E) ~1e6). gainSubstituted (X Newton step <= eps, K := ddGain(X), A-BK stable, row already within gainTol) is compliant: a float64 X converged to eps is its own re-certified iterate.

Amendment 4 (advisor, wave 43 O2MVDD review 2): am.3's terminal/substituted dd K applies only when the refinement runs on the unreduced problem (red == nil). On reduced inputs (m>n cheap control, red != nil or red.exact), the dd gain of the reduced problem (red.bw/rw/sw rounded to float64, mapped back by red.gain) loses cond*eps and is NOT the gain of the returned X: K must still pass gainMiss against the full-problem ddGain(X), or follow base's flow; reduced-problem refinement never produces a terminal K (refineDescriptorDare-terminal, gainSubstituted, steppedX all gated on red == nil). Evidence: rv39 13857 (native+amd64, K 6.5e-8 -> 2.73e-6 at Accuracy 0; head's K 40x off the 320-bit gain of its own X), 34852 (native, Accuracy 1 -> certified-wrong X 1.25e-8), 10831 (amd64, X exact, substituted K 4.7e-6 off while gain of X equals the oracle).

Amendment 4 evidence note (coordinator, wave 43 round 3): only 1 of am.4's 3 evidence rows holds against an E-exact 320-bit oracle. 13857 is a precision limit: w39Oracle rounds E^-1A/E^-1B to float64, which alone moves K 2.73e-6; a 1-ulp perturbation of Q moves K 2.6e-6; 7cd43f2 was 9e-13 natively. For 10831 the reduced ddGain equals the 320-bit gain of the returned X to 1e-16; the 4.72e-6 is the gain of the rounded X itself, so the "reduced-input precision loss" mechanism is wrong. 34852 is real. The gate stands as shipped (25716f9). Its cost: TestDareCrossTermGainOfConvergedX (5AFLTD, m>n) is loosened 1e-7 -> 1e-5, back to base. Narrowing the gate is a separate CORE task. Evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-josephj-workspace-controlsys/90f6527f-00fa-4f22-8ebb-64f8a65942a3/scratchpad/w43review/fixC/zz_fixc_13857_oracle_test.go.txt, zz_fixc_10831_gain_test.go.txt, /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-josephj-workspace-controlsys/90f6527f-00fa-4f22-8ebb-64f8a65942a3/scratchpad/w43review/rvD/zz_rvd_exact_test.go.

Amendment 5 (coordinator, wave 43 round 3): refineDescriptorDare's convergence measure xeX = max(Frobenius ratio, 1-norm ratio). It is monotone toward Accuracy 1, matches the oracles' 1-norm relErr, and was needed for 34852 (Frobenius 9.97e-9 while X was 1.25e-8 off in the 1-norm). Accepted although it went past the round-3 scope.

### am.6 (wave 47, TDFWXM; advisor ruling) — correction to am.4 evidence attribution
The old oracle's K errors (13857 2.73e-6, 37017 2.05e-4, 48867 7.36e-7, 41642 3.65e-6) came from forming K from the float64-rounded Y (dareDoublingBig returned hbDense(h)), not from rounding E^-1A/E^-1B (moves K ~1e-17 there). Rounding E^-1A does matter at cond(E)~1e7 (6e-10, 1e5x band). Oracle rule strengthened: keep E unrounded AND never form K from a rounded Y; stability checks of E-derived closed loops in extended precision. am.4 gate unchanged. In-repo reference: riccati_exact_descriptor_oracle_test.go.

### Wave 48 clarification (am.4, no logic change; coordinator-acked 2026-10-28)
- am.4's terminal dd K gate is to be read as not applying to red.rotated. With rotated inputs, V2 is empty and red.q = Q, so the problem is the given Dare under an orthogonal V, and its dd-refined K is terminal and sound. LU3SUY (#391) adds a persistent test. Routing that K through gainMiss produced 6 native and 8 amd64 ok->certified-wrong rows, plus about 770 Accuracy 0->1 drops. Evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-josephj-workspace-controlsys/90f6527f-00fa-4f22-8ebb-64f8a65942a3/scratchpad/w48review/lu3suy/.
- The unrefined rotated K (xe nil) is NOT covered by this clarification; see the wave-48 rotated-path followup.
- Record (D6QQX7, #391): against the exact-E oracle, none of the am.4 evidence rows' K errors is certified-wrong (13857, 10831 and 5AFLTD are all inside KBand; 34852 was an X defect). The gate's real cost was K errors up to 1e-4 at Accuracy 0 on about 1.5% of rv39 rows. hewerGainSubstituted recovers them (X kept, no terminal K), which is consistent with am.4.

### Wave 49 ruling (am.7, advisor 2026-10-28; V4OJPR question)
- am.4 holds at Accuracy 0. Never return a K that gainMiss rejects against the returned X, even when it is the extended-precision Hewer gain formed from the given unrounded A, B, Q, R, S, E. MATLAB idare's K is always the gain of its X.
- At Accuracy 1, return the converged Hewer K (instead of "nearest") when the reference converged. This removes the platform-dependent demoted K.
- Fail closed. A row that enters gainOfX at Accuracy 1 may be promoted to Accuracy 0 only if the extended reference converged AND agrees with K within its band. If the reference fails, the row stays at its incoming accuracy (cw->cw is allowed, acc1->cw is not). Seed 3 of rv49v (scratchpad/w49review/riccati-review/seed3_race_probe.txt) is the motivating acc1->cw row.
- Accepted cost: the V4OJPR experiment's cw->ok rows (6 native / 3 amd64) become cw->acc1.

### Wave 51 clarifications (advisor; coordinator-accepted 2026-10-28, #395 c054646)
1. am.4 and refined X: on rotated inputs X may move through refined()'s re-certified Newton step. That is am.1, the same path non-rotated inputs take. am.4 forbids replacing X with a terminal, dd or Hewer iterate; it does not forbid the certified step. Evidence: 15-20 rotated rows per sweep set; worst X error 3.7e-11 -> 1.9e-10; none outside the X band.
2. am.7 rule 2 scope: "at Accuracy 1, return the converged Hewer K" applies only when a Hewer reference was computed. Where the detector is gainMiss and no Hewer reference exists (rotated rows after #395; Hewer was the removed 10-16x cost), an Accuracy-1 row carries the best float64 K, as MATLAB idare does with Report 1. am.7 rule 1 (never return at Accuracy 0 a K gainMiss rejects) and fail-closed promotion are unchanged.

## Triage 53 advisor ruling (2026-10-29)
General policy (from WRVNNU, closed): when an Accuracy-0 X error exceeds the documented ~1e-8 Newton certification by 10% or less only in the 1-norm, and sits inside it in the Frobenius norm (WRVNNU seeds 895/1338: 1-norm 1.092e-8/1.048e-8, Frobenius 9.517e-9/9.877e-9, K 6.4e-16), it is certification-measure noise, not certified-wrong. Larger excess (e.g. 1.5e-8) cannot cite this. KXDOXH, closed: an honest error from a precision limit (H2Syn cheap-control, ‖K‖ 8e8, assembled closed loop +0.02 while A+B2F and A−LC2 are stable), pinned by TestRiccatiAccuracy_LqgH2Syn, is the honest direction under this rule; separation-structured H2Norm would be a feature. GXMPWS, closed as unreproducible: the headline Q/R/S literal is missing, and the best reconstruction gives honest Accuracy 1 on main (X 1.06e-9/1.16e-10, K 5.6e-7/1.9e-9). It was an X-certification row and is not covered by CEFUJP.

## Policy (wave 53, advisor): inseparable detector -> fail closed
When no float64 detector separates certified-wrong rows from near-band correct rows, the gate fails closed (Accuracy 1, best float64 K). Kept-cw outranks in-band demotion. In-band demotions are not regressions in that case; list each per row (seed, NS, base K, KBand) as a precision limit in the PR. Race builds are compared race-to-race and do not count toward native/amd64 flag-rate bars.

## Ruling (coordinator, post V4OJPR round 2): accepted Hewer K returns Accuracy 0
A7 says 0 means normwise-certified, and the next-iterate gain check is that certificate, whichever path produced K. This supersedes am.7 "Hewer K only at Accuracy 1". Separate from rv49v 1663 T, which is a false pass of the refined-K certificate.

title: Nyquist cluster merge/snap tolerances still use global cbrt(eps)·max|p|
body: Found in X34YEB; not fixed and no test yet. classifyNyquistBoundary (nyquist.go) still uses global tolerances for cluster merge and snap: bd.assign(..., 10*loose) and snap := max(loose, nyquistIndentBase), where loose = cbrt(eps)·max|p|. With a 1e10 pole, loose ≈ 6e4 rad, so a genuine boundary pole e^{jθ} next to it snaps to θ=0 or merges with other clusters. Possible repro: a discrete pole pair at e^{±j0.5} plus a pole at 1e10. Related residual: a defective small pole beside a huge pole still gets the global band, because the per-pole band is capped there. Done when: merge and snap use per-pole scaling like the X34YEB bands, the repro gives RHP/boundary counts matching the oracle, and existing Nyquist tests pass.

title: LOW: exact finite-count Jacobi floor (A5a) if the 320-bit staircase is revived
body:
Revive-only note carried from T73RLU (done) so it stays live: applies only if the 320-bit exact finite-count path (parked/polesdetail-wave56 71fa939, poles_finite_count_exact.go) is ever brought back. PolesDetail #412 (c2dfa64) shipped without it.


## Carried from T73RLU (verbatim)
## A5 check result (2026-10-31, read-only probe on parked/polesdetail-wave56 71fa939; no code change)
Probe: the poles_detail_test.go integer-chain generator with PCG(3,30), 60 runs (nf=1+run%3, k=1+(run/3)%3), with jacobiRows instrumented in a throwaway worktree. Result: 17/60 "Jacobi unconverged on σ₁" (record said 18/60; the difference is the generator variant). Every cap hit is on σ₁ of an exactly singular integer E.
Mechanism: exactJacobiStop is RELATIVE (γ² ≤ 2^-600·α·β, cos ≤ 2^-300), not absolute. For an exact zero singular value, one row converges to zero geometrically but never reaches it, because big.Float has an unbounded exponent:
- |q|² goes 4e-9 at sweep 2 → binary exponent −10664 at sweep 20 → −61380 at sweep 99.
- That row stays a rounding image of row 0 (cos² = 1 at every sweep), so the relative test can never pass. All other pairs are converged by sweep 20 (cos² ≤ 2^-185).
So the two accepted constants are inconsistent: a relative stop under unbounded-exponent arithmetic cannot certify a numerically null row.
Proposed ruled change (no data tolerance): add a working-precision floor to the pair test, derived from exactCountPrec. A pair counts as converged when γ² ≤ 2^-600·α·β OR min(α,β) ≤ 2^(-2·exactCountPrec)·max_i‖x_i‖² (the smaller row is below the 320-bit floor of the matrix). Such a row's singular value is ≤ 2^-320·σ₁ ≪ τ_E = n·eps(σ₁), so no deflation count can change. Expected: 0/60 cap hits and identical brackets; to be verified by the fixer, not measured.

## Ruling A5a (coordinator, 2026-10-31): APPROVED
The working-precision floor in the Jacobi pair test is a convergence control, not a data tolerance; it has the same shape as boundaryCertified's band. A pair is converged when γ² ≤ 2^-600·α·β OR min(α,β) ≤ 2^(-2·exactCountPrec)·max_i‖x_i‖².
Fixer conditions:
- 0 cap hits on the 60 exact pencils.
- Brackets bit-identical to 71fa939 on every row that converged there, across all 1522 rows on both arches.
- Any remaining cap hit gets Accuracy 1 with bracket [0,n].
- The floor is defined in production code next to exactCountPrec.
The fixer is HELD until the user rules on the field shape (A6).

title: EDGE: Mixsyn errors 'gamma not achievable' on numerically singular square static G
body:

[w13 #44 riccati/IZKUS3] Mixsyn errors on a square, numerically singular static G when the slow-weight pole is not near z=1, continuous or discrete. Mixsyn returns 'γ = 1.4e12 not achievable' for dt = 1, 0.1, 1e-2 and 1e-4, and for the continuous analog W1 = ss(-0.1, 1, 9.95, 0.5).
